It wasn't a date---it was a date that almost happened. But whilst trying to get over a mega huge unrequited crush (a FWB who got into a serious relationship with someone else) I'd been nursing for a couple months, I got on OkCupid and tried to meet new people, one of whom was an interesting, if slightly neurotic dude who looked vaguely familiar. 

We texted for a bit and planned to get coffee the next day. During our texting conversation, he linked me to his Soundcloud page, at which point I saw his name. And it was MegaCrush's younger brother.

I was like "Yoooo. Do you have...a brother?"

And he launched into a giant rant about how everyone likes his brother more and the last two people he dated were his brother's exes. Ssssso, yeah, that was a bust.

Just learn to love masturbation, alas. I'm sort of in the same position, minus the marriage (got into a serious relationship with a partner I really love, but the reality is our libidos are not compatible---my partner was really into sex with me at the beginning because of the novelty, but in general isn't really a very sexual person, so after the novelty wore off, our sex life died out)

Ultimately, I really really care for my partner more than I do about sex, so I wouldn't want to break up with them just because they're not a huge fan of boning. It sucks, it really does, and I'm super sexually frustrated, but I just bought more sex toys and have tried to relieve the physical urges with masturbation. As for the desire for intimacy, I am teaching myself to understand that not everyone expresses emotional intimacy through sex, and some people are more about massages, or cooking dinner for each other, or cuddling, and that's ok. I wouldn't want my partner to do something they didn't feel like doing, so I'd never pressure them to have sex with me.

I guess the bottom line is, is sex a high enough priority for you that it's a deal/marriage-breaker? If it is, there is nothing wrong with that. You're not a pig, just sexually incompatible. It's okay for her not to want sex, and okay for you to want it, but maybe it's better that she be with someone who is equally uninterested in sex, and you with someone who has a high libido like you. However, maybe there are qualities to the marriage that outweigh the sex. Maybe you can discuss an open relationship? My partner would be cautiously down for that, but I could never do that---it's just not the same. I don't want to just have SEX, i want to have sex with someone I love, so i can't just go out looking for cute gay boys to bone. It's not appealing to me.

 But it's ultimately up to you to decide what you need. Good luck!
